A_target.statement:
Let $M$ be a [[Definition:Smooth Manifold|smooth manifold]].
Then there are well-defined operations $\d: \map {\Omega^k} M \to \map {\Omega^{k + 1} } M$ and $\wedge$ on [[Definition:Differential Form|differential forms]] on $M$, with:
:$\d \circ \d = 0$
and if $M$ is [[Definition:Oriented Manifold|oriented]] and [[Definition:Compact Manifold|compact]] with boundary:
:$\displaystyle \int_M \d \omega = \int_{\partial M} \omega$

B_source.statement:
Let $U \subseteq \R^n$ be [[Definition:Open Set (Real Analysis)|open]].
A [[Definition:Differential Form|differential $k$-form]] on $U$ is $\omega = \displaystyle \sum_I f_I \rd x_I$, with [[Definition:Exterior Derivative|exterior derivative]]:
:$\displaystyle \d \omega = \sum_I \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n \frac {\partial f_I} {\partial x_j} \rd x_j \wedge \d x_I$

substitutions.the open subset of Euclidean space: a chart domain on the manifold
substitutions.the coordinate definition of the exterio: the same definition, applied within each chart
substitutions.the identity map between overlapping dom: the transition map between overlapping charts

derived.the exterior derivative: well defined globally, because it commutes with pullback along transitions
derived.the wedge product: likewise globally defined, being pointwise and coordinate independent

object_map.reformulation: Apply the Euclidean definitions chartwise and check they agree on overlaps, so they glue to a global object.

validity_conditions: The exterior derivative commutes with pullback along smooth maps, which is exactly what makes the coordinate definitions agree on chart overlaps.
Agreement on overlaps is what upgrades a family of local definitions into a single global one; without it the construction would depend on the atlas.
Orientability is required for integration of top forms and hence for the global Stokes theorem, even though the exterior derivative itself needs no orientation.
proof_plan: On each [[Definition:Chart|chart]] $\tuple {U, \phi}$ of $M$, define forms, $\wedge$ and $\d$ by the Euclidean formulas on $\map \phi U$.

Let $\tau$ be a [[Definition:Transition Map|transition map]] between overlapping charts.
The Euclidean $\d$ and $\wedge$ commute with [[Definition:Pullback of Differential Form|pullback]]:
:$\map {\tau^*} {\d \omega} = \d \paren {\tau^* \omega}$
so the local definitions agree on overlaps.

Glue the local definitions into global operations on $M$.
The identity $\d \circ \d = 0$ holds locally, by [[Symmetry of Second Derivatives|symmetry of second derivatives]], hence globally.
